note: Seed bank for IGNOU CLIS Dec 2026. Grow it by extracting questions from real PYQs downloaded with scripts/fetch_materials.py.

questions.question: Who propounded the Five Laws of Library Science?
questions.explanation: Dr. S. R. Ranganathan stated the Five Laws in 1931.

questions.question: 'Books are for use' is which law of library science?
questions.explanation: First Law: Books are for use.

questions.question: Weeding out damaged and obsolete books is an application of which law?
questions.explanation: Fifth Law: a library is a growing organism - growth includes weeding.

questions.question: Introducing an open access system in a library mainly follows from which law?
questions.explanation: Open access saves the reader's time (Fourth Law).

questions.question: Deciding a library's location and working hours so people can use it easily is an application of which law?
questions.explanation: Convenient location and hours make books usable - First Law.

questions.question: 'Every reader his or her book' is which law?
questions.explanation: Second Law: every reader his/her book.

questions.question: In which year was Ranganathan's 'Five Laws of Library Science' first published?
questions.explanation: First published in 1931.

questions.question: The National Library of India is located at:
questions.explanation: The National Library of India is in Kolkata.

questions.question: A public library is primarily financed from:
questions.explanation: Public libraries are maintained out of public funds and open to all.

questions.question: A library serving a specialised user group such as a research institute is a:
questions.explanation: Special libraries serve a specific subject or user community.

questions.question: The accession register records:
options: Documents acquired by the library, in accession-number order
questions.explanation: It is the chronological master record of every document added to the library.

questions.question: Before ordering a newly requested book, the acquisition section first checks:
options: Whether the book is already in the library (duplicate checking)
The market price of other libraries
questions.explanation: Duplicate checking avoids buying copies the library already holds.

questions.question: In the Browne charging system, the reader borrows books using:
options: A date slip and book card
questions.explanation: Browne: the book's pocket is placed in the borrower's ticket.

questions.question: The Newark charging system uses:
options: A date slip and book card
questions.explanation: Newark: due date stamped on the date slip; the book card records the loan.

questions.question: How many digits does an ISBN assigned after 2007 have?
questions.explanation: ISBNs have been 13 digits since 2007 (earlier 10).

questions.question: Technical processing of a newly acquired document mainly consists of:
questions.explanation: Technical processing = classifying and cataloguing before the book reaches the shelf.

questions.question: In DDC, the main class 000 covers:
questions.explanation: 000 = computer science, information and generalities.

questions.question: In DDC, the main class 100 is:
questions.explanation: 100 = philosophy and psychology.

questions.question: In DDC, religion is class:
questions.explanation: 200 = religion.

questions.question: In DDC, the social sciences are class:
questions.explanation: 300 = social sciences.

questions.question: In DDC, class 500 covers:
questions.explanation: 500 = pure/natural sciences and mathematics.

questions.question: In DDC, medicine falls under:
questions.explanation: 610 = medicine and health, inside 600 technology/applied sciences.

questions.question: In DDC, literature is class:
questions.explanation: 800 = literature; 700 is arts & recreation.

questions.question: In DDC, history and geography are class:
questions.explanation: 900 = history and geography.

questions.question: The Dewey Decimal Classification was devised by:
questions.explanation: Melvil Dewey published DDC's first edition in 1876.

questions.question: How many main classes does DDC have?
questions.explanation: Ten main classes, 000 to 900.

questions.question: Under AACR-2R, the main entry for a work by a single personal author is made under:
questions.explanation: Main entry is under the person chiefly responsible - the author.

questions.question: In AACR-2R, an 'added entry' is:
options: Any entry other than the main entry (e.g. title, subject, collaborator)
questions.explanation: Added entries give extra access points beyond the main entry.

questions.question: In MARC21, the tag 245 records:
questions.explanation: 245 = title statement; 100 = main personal name.

questions.question: In MARC21, the ISBN is recorded in tag:
questions.explanation: 020 = International Standard Book Number.

questions.question: The Classified Catalogue Code (CCC) was developed by:
questions.explanation: CCC is Ranganathan's catalogue code.

questions.question: Shelf rectification means:
options: Checking shelves and restoring books to their correct order
questions.explanation: Rectification = reading the shelf order and correcting misplaced books.

questions.question: A patent, thesis or research report is a:
questions.explanation: Original first-hand research output = primary source.

questions.question: An encyclopedia is a:
questions.explanation: Encyclopedias compile and arrange published knowledge - secondary.

questions.question: A bibliography of bibliographies is a:
questions.explanation: It guides you to secondary sources - tertiary.

questions.question: A dictionary is generally treated as a:
questions.explanation: Dictionaries, encyclopedias and textbooks are secondary sources.

questions.question: The main role of tertiary sources is to:
options: Guide the user to primary and secondary sources
questions.explanation: Tertiary sources (e.g. bibliography of bibliographies, directory of directories) point to other sources.

questions.question: A newspaper is generally regarded as a:
questions.explanation: Newspapers carry first-hand current reporting - primary.

questions.question: 'The World of Learning' is a:
questions.explanation: It lists universities, colleges and learned bodies worldwide.

questions.question: A yearbook mainly provides:
options: Facts and statistics of a particular year
questions.explanation: Yearbooks are annual compendia of facts and trends.

questions.question: SDI stands for:
questions.explanation: SDI pushes new information matching a user's profile.

questions.question: CAS in library services stands for:
questions.explanation: CAS keeps users aware of new developments in their field.

questions.question: Ready reference service deals with:
options: Fact-finding questions answered quickly from ready-reference sources
questions.explanation: Short factual answers from dictionaries, yearbooks, directories, etc.

questions.question: Long-range reference service typically involves:
options: Prepared searches such as bibliographies, done over a longer time
questions.explanation: Long-range service needs extended search time and compiled outputs.

questions.question: An indexing or abstracting periodical is a:
questions.explanation: It arranges and points to primary literature - secondary.

questions.question: In circulation work, 'discharging' means:
options: Issuing a book to a member
Recording the return of a borrowed document and cancelling the loan record
questions.explanation: Charging = recording the issue; discharging = recording the return.

questions.question: User orientation in a library aims at:
options: Introducing new users to the library's resources, services and rules
questions.explanation: Orientation (user education) familiarises readers with the library.

questions.question: Reference books such as encyclopedias and dictionaries in the reference section are usually:
options: Meant for consultation inside the library, not issued
questions.explanation: Ready-reference works stay in the library so they are always available.

questions.question: Koha is:
options: An open-source Integrated Library Management System (ILS)
questions.explanation: Koha is a free, open-source ILS used for library automation.

questions.question: OPAC stands for:
questions.explanation: The OPAC lets users search the library catalogue online.

questions.question: Koha was first developed in:
questions.explanation: Koha originated in New Zealand (Katipo Communications, 1999-2000).

questions.question: SOUL (Software for University Libraries) was developed by:
questions.explanation: SOUL is INFLIBNET's library management software.

questions.question: Library automation primarily means computerising:
options: Housekeeping operations: acquisition, cataloguing, circulation and serials control
questions.explanation: Automation covers all housekeeping operations, not just the catalogue.

questions.question: RFID technology in libraries is mainly used for:
options: Self check-in/check-out and fast stock verification
questions.explanation: RFID tags identify items by radio waves - quick issue, return and shelf audit.

questions.question: A barcode on a library book normally encodes its:
questions.explanation: The barcode stores the item's accession number for circulation.

questions.question: Ubuntu is:
options: An open-source operating system (a Linux distribution)
questions.explanation: Ubuntu is a free Linux-based operating system.

questions.question: In LibreOffice, the word-processing application equivalent to MS Word is:
questions.explanation: Writer = documents, Calc = spreadsheets, Impress = presentations.

questions.question: PDF stands for:
questions.explanation: Portable Document Format.

questions.question: LAN stands for:
questions.explanation: A LAN connects computers within a limited area such as a building.

questions.question: A search engine such as Google works by:
options: Storing all web pages on your computer
Indexing web pages and retrieving matches for a query
questions.explanation: Search engines crawl and index the web, then match your keywords.

questions.question: Web 2.0 is characterised by:
options: User participation and interaction (blogs, wikis, social networking)
questions.explanation: Web 2.0 = the participatory, interactive web.

questions.question: DSpace is:
questions.explanation: DSpace builds institutional/digital repositories (eGyankosh itself runs on it).

questions.question: A digital library is:
options: A library with only printed books
A collection of documents in organised electronic form, accessible online
questions.explanation: Digital libraries store and serve documents in electronic form.

questions.question: Greenstone is:
questions.explanation: Greenstone is free software for building digital library collections.
